description: The line plot illustrates the relationship between the co-occurrence number (x-axis) and the accuracy (ACC, %) (y-axis) for six different methods: Base, FT, IKE, MEND, MEMIT, and ROME. The x-axis, labeled “Co-occurrence Number,” is displayed on a logarithmic scale ranging from 10⁰ to 10³, with major tick marks at 10⁰, 10¹, 10², and 10³. The y-axis, labeled “ACC (%)”, is linear and spans from 60% to 85%, with major gridlines and tick labels at 60, 65, 70, 75, 80, and 85. All six lines show a generally increasing trend in accuracy as co-occurrence number increases. The green line with square markers (ROME) starts at approximately 74.5% at 10⁰ and rises to about 82.5% at 10³. The brown line with diamond markers (MEND) begins near 68% at 10⁰ and reaches approximately 81% at 10³. The purple line with circle markers (MEMIT) starts around 68.5% and ends near 80%. The red line with triangle markers (IKE) begins at about 66.5% and increases to roughly 79%. The blue line with downward-pointing triangle markers (FT) starts at approximately 64.5% and rises to about 78.5%. The black line with circle markers (Base) begins at roughly 63% and ends near 77.5%. All lines exhibit a steeper slope at lower co-occurrence numbers and gradually flatten as the co-occurrence number increases.
